newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Doosan Group to streamline affiliates.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Doosan Group to streamline affiliates.

text.p: Doosan Group, South Korea's 14th-largest conglomerate, said on Tuesday it would cut the number of its affiliates from 25 to a minimum of 19 by the end of next year through mergers and sales as part of a restructuring drive.
The group's spokesman told Reuters OB Brewery Co's planned absorption of Doo San Beverage Co was part of the restructuring drive.
"We have promoted the restructuring plan from several years ago according to changes in the business environment," Kim Jin, Doosan's director of public information, said by telephone.
Kim said OB Brewery was expected to record a net profit of 35 billion won in calendar 1997 on turnover of 1.7 trillion won after the merger.
In 1996, OB Brewery recorded a net loss of 96.41 billion won while Doo San Beverage posted 3.57 billion won of net profit.
"OB Brewery had already been expected to post a net profit this year as the company's share of the domestic beer market was recovering," Kim said.
OB Brewery ran net losses during the past three consecutive years, which analysts have attributed to growing marketing costs to defend against intensified challenges by rival makers.
Kim declined to name affiliates to be merged or sold off.
